# 2 Clement — Chapter 13 (SOPHIA Consensus)

**Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Clement 13
**Agent:** SOPHIA (Consensus)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Consensus Translation

1. So then, brothers, at last let us repent; let us be sober unto what is good; for we are full of much foolishness and wickedness. Let us wipe out from ourselves our former sins, and repenting with our whole soul, be saved.
2. And let us not be people-pleasers or wish to please only ourselves, but by our righteous conduct let us please also those who are outside, so that the Name may not be blasphemed because of us.
3. For the Lord says: "My name is being blasphemed continually among all the nations," and again: "Woe to him because of whom my name is blasphemed." In what way is it blasphemed? In that you do not do what I wish.
4. For when the Gentiles hear from our mouths the oracles of God, they marvel at their beauty and greatness; but then, discovering that our works do not match our words, they turn from admiration to blasphemy, saying that it is a myth and a delusion.
5. For when they hear from us that God says: "It is no credit to you if you love those who love you, but it is a credit to you if you love your enemies and those who hate you" — hearing this, they marvel at the surpassing goodness; but when they see that we do not love even those who hate us, but only those who love us, they scoff at us and the Name is blasphemed.

---

## Council Notes

- v.3: The first quote is from Isaiah 52:5 / Ezekiel 36:23 (LXX). "My name is blasphemed among the nations" is a prophetic refrain that the preacher applies to Christian hypocrisy — a sharp self-critical move.
- v.5: The "love your enemies" teaching is a form of Matthew 5:46-47 / Luke 6:32-33, attributed here directly to God (*ho theos legei*), not to Jesus — possibly a liturgical/catechetical transmission where the teaching was understood as divine speech.
- vv.4-5: The argument that Christian inconsistency causes Gentile blasphemy is also found in Paul (Rom 2:24, citing Isa 52:5). The preacher may draw on Paul here.
